sentences.text: Millerosteus was a small placoderm, an extinct armored fish, that grew to only 14 cm in length. It is one of the few arthrodire genera known from specimens preserving the entire skeleton.
The genus Millerosteus was described by Stensiö in 1959 based on fossils found in Orkney and Caithness, Scotland.

Millerosteus is classified within the class Placodermi as an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm. It belongs to the family Coccosteidae, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the superclade Eubrachythoraci.
This animal lived during the Early Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period, with fossils dating from 393.47 to 382.31 million years ago.
